title: Sergeant Major-First Sergeant (SgtMaj to 1stSgt) PMOS, DC M&RA
raw_text:
6.     MOS 8999, Sergeant Major-First Sergeant (SgtMaj to 1stSgt) PMOS, DC M&RA

    a. Summary. The Command Senior Enlisted Leader is responsible to the
commander for all matters which effect the morale, welfare, discipline,
mission success, and overall readiness of the unit. They disseminate and
enforce Marine Corps and local policies, orders, and directives. They
possess comprehensive knowledge of Marine Corps organization, history,
traditions, customs and courtesies. They are directly responsible for all
enlisted career human resource matters within the unit and have a mandate to
maintain and develop the total force.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Security requirement:

                (a) Top secret clearance required for sergeant major.

                (b) Secret security clearance required for first sergeant.

            (2) Possess a high degree of physical and mental resilience.




                                           3-509                           Enclosure (1)
 3156                                                               NAVMC 1200.1L



            (3) Ability to obtain situational awareness and think critically.

            (4) Ability to communicate effectively both orally and in writing.

        (5) Demonstrate an ability to multitask and manage shifting
priorities.

        (6) Must have requested to be considered for 1stSgt on latest fitness
report by typing an “F” in item 8h.

        (7) Exhibit a consistent and exemplary standard of military
appearance, physical fitness, and personal discipline.

        (8) Possess a high degree of moral character, ethical standards,
embodies our core values, leadership traits and principles.

       c.   Requirements

            (1) Elected to 1stSgt or SgtMaj by an enlisted promotion board.

            (2) 1stSgts are required to attend E-8 PME requirements.

            (3) 1stSgts are required to attend 1stSgt school.

            (4) SgtMajs are required to attend E-9 PME requirements.

       d.   Duties

            (1) 1stSgt:

            (a) Serve as the unit senior enlisted leader (USEL) and subject
matter expert to the commander on the responsibilities of command and
institutional standards.

            (b) Communicates commander’s intent and facilitates personnel and
professional development.

            (c) Assist the commander in creating a positive command climate
and institutional culture with a focus on readiness, mission, diversity,
inclusion, and accountability.

            (d) Supervise, inspect, and enforce standards relating to good
order and discipline, the conduct of drill and ceremonies, military
appearance, customs and courtesies.

            (e) Responsible for the administrative correctness of all
enlisted performance evaluations and assists in ensuring the timeliness of
the command’s fitness reports and junior enlisted evaluations.

            (f) Ensures the timely and accurate completion of administrative
tasks in support of internal and external correspondence, awards, promotions,
MCTFS reporting, and request mast.

            (g) Disseminate and enforce all applicable orders and policies
throughout the organization.

            (h) Assist in the development and management of professional
relationships.



                                        3-510                          Enclosure (1)
 3156                                                           NAVMC 1200.1L



            (i) Supervise all personnel matters (i.e. force preservation,
quality of life issues, personal and professional development and readiness).

            (j) Screen personnel within the command for assignment to special
duty assignments, screen able “B” billets and overseas assignments.

            (k) Conduct, supervise and manage enlisted professional education
including non-resident and resident PME, unit PME program, annual training
requirements and professional reading program.

            (l) Assist commander in the operational mission of the unit.

            (m) Assist the commander in the sustainment of unit readiness
through all functions of command.

            (n) Review and advise on legal process’ residing with the unit
commander or higher.

            (o) Assume any additional duties as directed by the commander.

        (2) In addition to those duties expected of a 1stSgt, SgtMajs (04 &
05 command level):

            (a) Fully understand orders, regulations, and doctrinal
publications applicable to the command in order to assist the commander in
shaping policy.

            (b) Assist the commander with, retention, career development,
retirement and separations of all Marines in the command.

            (c) Provide oversight and ensure compliance of the unit’s single
Marine program.

            (d) Assist in the mentorship and development of the unit’s
enlisted and officers.

            (e) Provide oversight of the unit’s Prevention Programs and
utilization of available services.

            (f) Assist in the development of staff personnel, special staff,
and collateral duty billet holders.

            (g) Provide oversight of the command inspection program and any
external inspections.

            (h) Assist the Commander with the proper manning and resourcing
of personnel throughout subordinate units.

            (i) Develop, supervise, and train subordinate unit leaders in the
proper execution of drill, ceremonies, and protocol.

            (j) Create professional military education opportunities for
Marines within the unit.

            (k) Assume other duties as designated by the commander and higher
headquarters.




                                    3-511                        Enclosure (1)
 3156                                                               NAVMC 1200.1L



        (3) In addition to those duties expected at the 1stSgt and 04/05
level, SgtMajs (06 command level):

            (a) Interact with higher headquarters in order to advocate for
the needs of subordinate units.

            (b) Interpret and implement higher headquarters policies within
mission requirements of subordinate units.

            (c) Cultivate a positive and non-biased professional relationship
and open lines of communication with subordinate command teams.

            (d) Review and advise on legal process’ unique to commanders with
courts martial convening authority.

            (e) Mentor and develop subordinate unit senior enlisted and
commanders and advise on complex unit and personnel challenges.

            (f) Must be familiar with the titles, authorities, budget, and
permissions applicable to the command and its mission.

            (g) Develop a familiarity with the joint, interagency,
intergovernmental, multinational (JIIM) environment and diplomacy,
information, military, and economic (DIME) considerations.

               (h) Assume other duties as designated by the commander and higher
headquarter.

        (4) In addition to those duties expected at all previous levels,
SgtMajs (general/flag officer level):

               (a) Advise in the development of the command inspection program.

            (b) Must be well versed in the commanders’ and CMC strategic
messaging campaign.

            (c) Be familiar with strategic level documents (i.e., national
defense strategy, national military strategy).

            (d) Assist the commander with policies affecting DOD civilians
and contractors in support of the command.

               (e) Understanding general officer protocols and professional
ethics.

            (f) Develop a functional understanding of the JIIM environment
and DIME/PMESII considerations.

               (g) Assume other duties as designated by the general officer.

    e.      Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
None.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   None.

4001.   IMPLEMENTATION OF MOS CONVERSION

1.   Deputy Commandant, Manpower and Reserve Affairs

    a. Director, Manpower Plans (DC M&RA (MP)).      Modify models to reflect
MOS changes shown in figure 4-1.

    b. Director, Personnel Management Division (DC M&RA (MM)). Modify
models and other supporting information systems to reflect MOS changes shown
in figure 4-1. The Type Transaction Code (TTC) conversion for the Marine
Corps Total Force System (MCTFS) will convert MOSs (BMOS) and (PMOS) and add
requisite non-PMOS (as applicable) for active-duty components. Action will
be accomplished by the DC M&RA (MM) on 1 October 2025 to convert the present
MOS codes being revised as listed in the table of MOSs to the new MOS codes
listed (refer to figure 4-1).

    c. Director, Management Information Systems Division. Update the MCTFS
MOS tables prior to the DC M&RA (MM, RA) submission of the TTC conversions
that will occur on 1 October 2025.

2. Commanding General, Marine Corps Recruiting Command. Ensure MOS
conversions are entered into the Marine Corps Recruit Information Support
System (MCRISS) on 15 January 2025.

3. Commanding General, Training and Education Command. Conduct a final
coordination meeting and then release an advisory to marine forces, which
will announce revision of this Manual and serve as the source document on 15
January 2025.

4. Director, Total Force Structure Division (DC CD&I (TFS)). Update Total
Force Structure Management System (TFSMS) to reflect the MOS conversions
contained in figure 4-1 in or about February 2025.

5. Commanding General, Training and Education Command. CG TECOM, Policy and
Standards Division, will release an advisory to marine forces, which will
serve as the source document on 15 April 2025.

6.   Marine Corps Reserve

    a. DC M&RA (RA). Coordinate retraining of Prior Service MOS Retraining
Program” (PSMRP) Marines and Active Reserve (AR) Marines as required for MOS
conversion, subject to the availability of funds.

    b. The Commander, Marine Forces Reserve (COMMARFORRES). Coordinate
retraining of SMCR Marines as required for MOS conversion, subject to the
availability of funds.

    c. The Commanding General (CG), Individual Reserve Support Organization
(MIRSO). Make appropriate SRB entries for Individual Mobilization
Augmentees, Individual Ready Reservists, and Standby Reservists using as
authority the DC M&RA (MM) conversion action appearing on the RUC's DFR with
an origin of "HQ".

4002.   COMMANDING OFFICER'S RESPONSIBILITIES

1. Active component units verify appropriate conversion actions appearing on
the RUC's Diary Feedback Report (DFR) with an origin code of "HQ".

2. Commanding Officers will ensure that no unit diary entries are submitted
based on the revisions of this Manual until after the 1 October 2025 batch
change performed by DC M&RA (MM). Omissions from the batch changes should be
coordinated with DC M&RA (MM) before changes are submitted by the unit.

3. Directors of Marine Corps formal schools and commanders of training
detachments will award current MOSs until directed by MARADMIN to implement
new conversions (usually coinciding with new fiscal year).

occupation_text: 6. MOS 8999, Sergeant Major-First Sergeant (SgtMaj to 1stSgt) PMOS, DC M&RA a. Summary. The Command Senior Enlisted Leader is responsible to the commander for all matters which effect the morale, welfare, discipline, mission success, and overall readiness of the unit. They disseminate and enforce Marine Corps and local policies, orders, and directives. They possess comprehensive knowledge of Marine Corps organization, history, traditions, customs and courtesies. They are directly responsible for all enlisted career human resource matters within the unit and have a mandate to maintain and develop the total force. b. Prerequisites (1) Security requirement: (a) Top secret clearance required for sergeant major. (b) Secret security clearance required for first sergeant. (2) Possess a high degree of physical and mental resilience. (3) Ability to obtain situational awareness and think critically. (4) Ability to communicate effectively both orally and in writing. (5) Demonstrate an ability to multitask and manage shifting priorities. (6) Must have requested to be considered for 1stSgt on latest fitness report by typing an “F” in item 8h. (7) Exhibit a consistent and exemplary standard of military appearance, physical fitness, and personal discipline. (8) Possess a high degree of moral character, ethical standards, embodies our core values, leadership traits and principles. c. Requirements (1) Elected to 1stSgt or SgtMaj by an enlisted promotion board. (2) 1stSgts are required to attend E-8 PME requirements. (3) 1stSgts are required to attend 1stSgt school. (4) SgtMajs are required to attend E-9 PME requirements. d. Duties (1) 1stSgt: (a) Serve as the unit senior enlisted leader (USEL) and subject matter expert to the commander on the responsibilities of command and institutional standards. (b) Communicates commander’s intent and facilitates personnel and professional development. (c) Assist the commander in creating a positive command climate and institutional culture with a focus on readiness, mission, diversity, inclusion, and accountability. (d) Supervise, inspect, and enforce standards relating to good order and discipline, the conduct of drill and ceremonies, military appearance, customs and courtesies. (e) Responsible for the administrative correctness of all enlisted performance evaluations and assists in ensuring the timeliness of the command’s fitness reports and junior enlisted evaluations. (f) Ensures the timely and accurate completion of administrative tasks in support of internal and external correspondence, awards, promotions, MCTFS reporting, and request mast. (g) Disseminate and enforce all applicable orders and policies throughout the organization. (h) Assist in the development and management of professional relationships. (i) Supervise all personnel matters (i.e. force preservation, quality of life issues, personal and professional development and readiness). (j) Screen personnel within the command for assignment to special duty assignments, screen able “B” billets and overseas assignments. (k) Conduct, supervise and manage enlisted professional education including non-resident and resident PME, unit PME program, annual training requirements and professional reading program. (l) Assist commander in the operational mission of the unit. (m) Assist the commander in the sustainment of unit readiness through all functions of command. (n) Review and advise on legal process’ residing with the unit commander or higher. (o) Assume any additional duties as directed by the commander. (2) In addition to those duties expected of a 1stSgt, SgtMajs (04 & 05 command level): (a) Fully understand orders, regulations, and doctrinal publications applicable to the command in order to assist the commander in shaping policy. (b) Assist the commander with, retention, career development, retirement and separations of all Marines in the command. (c) Provide oversight and ensure compliance of the unit’s single Marine program. (d) Assist in the mentorship and development of the unit’s enlisted and officers. (e) Provide oversight of the unit’s Prevention Programs and utilization of available services. (f) Assist in the development of staff personnel, special staff, and collateral duty billet holders. (g) Provide oversight of the command inspection program and any external inspections. (h) Assist the Commander with the proper manning and resourcing of personnel throughout subordinate units. (i) Develop, supervise, and train subordinate unit leaders in the proper execution of drill, ceremonies, and protocol. (j) Create professional military education opportunities for Marines within the unit. (k) Assume other duties as designated by the commander and higher headquarters. (3) In addition to those duties expected at the 1stSgt and 04/05 level, SgtMajs (06 command level): (a) Interact with higher headquarters in order to advocate for the needs of subordinate units. (b) Interpret and implement higher headquarters policies within mission requirements of subordinate units. (c) Cultivate a positive and non-biased professional relationship and open lines of communication with subordinate command teams. (d) Review and advise on legal process’ unique to commanders with courts martial convening authority. (e) Mentor and develop subordinate unit senior enlisted and commanders and advise on complex unit and personnel challenges. (f) Must be familiar with the titles, authorities, budget, and permissions applicable to the command and its mission. (g) Develop a familiarity with the joint, interagency, intergovernmental, multinational (JIIM) environment and diplomacy, information, military, and economic (DIME) considerations. (h) Assume other duties as designated by the commander and higher headquarter. (4) In addition to those duties expected at all previous levels, SgtMajs (general/flag officer level): (a) Advise in the development of the command inspection program. (b) Must be well versed in the commanders’ and CMC strategic messaging campaign. (c) Be familiar with strategic level documents (i.e., national defense strategy, national military strategy). (d) Assist the commander with policies affecting DOD civilians and contractors in support of the command. (e) Understanding general officer protocols and professional ethics. (f) Develop a functional understanding of the JIIM environment and DIME/PMESII considerations. (g) Assume other duties as designated by the general officer.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
